AS3MT: transcripts, DNA and RNA-seq

Source: vignettes/as3mt-splice-variants-demo.Rmd
as3mt-splice-variants-demo.Rmd

Load the example

Compare human full-length AS3MT, a paper-defined d2d3 reconstruction, and chimpanzee full-length AS3MT. Coordinates use GRCh38 and Pan_tro_3.0, respectively. All inputs are bundled; no downloads are needed.

library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)
demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "as3mt", package = "ggexon")
source(file.path(demo_dir, "load-as3mt-example.R"), local = TRUE)
as3mt <- load_as3mt_example(demo_dir)

1. Transcripts and compressed introns

geom_exon2() shows CDS as thick boxes and UTR as thin boxes. Keep the full-reference exon numbering: d2d3 retains E1 and E4–E11; dashed boxes mark skipped E2/E3. scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 30) compresses introns 30-fold while keeping exon widths. geom_nuclink() automatically follows that same piecewise scale in both annotation panels. The build trains the maps from exon layers first, then applies them to related genomic layers; adding coverage or labels does not change the exon/intron boundaries.

as3mt_plot <- plot_as3mt_example(as3mt, intron_factor = 30)
as3mt_plot$plot

Transcript comparison; introns compressed 30-fold.

The helper uses this grammar:

ggexon(as3mt$comparison) +
  geom_exon2(aes(xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5,
    ymin = isoform_y, transcripts = transcript_name, fill = exon_class),
    annotation_type = "all", compress_introns = FALSE,
    utr_height = 0.35, cds_height = 1) +
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "human_chimp", aes(fill = identity_band),
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_genomics(vars(track), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 30,
    guide = guide_x_ggexon_piecewise(by = "panel"))

Ribbons retain the two highest LASTZ identity categories, 97.1–98.3% and 98.3–100%. The 37 ungapped blocks split into 57 polygon pieces at scale boundaries. They show DNA similarity, not expression or proof of exon skipping.

2. DNA detail at the exon-1 repeat

The selected human reference contains three 36-bp VNTR units; the chimp reference has one imperfect homolog (34/36 matching bases). The terminal unit contains 24 exonic and 12 intronic bases. Both references retain the GT donor:

CCTGAGTCGCAGGCCGAGGAGACA | GTGAGTGCGCGC
         human exon 1  | intron 1

Prepare two aligned strings with an explicitly named human reference. - denotes a gap and does not consume genomic bases. The strings are verified against the bundled FASTAs; the donor-anchored alignment places 72 chimp gap columns opposite two human repeat copies.

v <- readRDS(file.path(demo_dir, "vntr-dna.rds"))
sequence_data <- alignseq_data(v$aligned, v$anchors, reference = "human",
  regions = v$regions, details = v$details, flank = 0)

geom_alignseq() places each species’ DNA on its own panel. Default markers show differences, with DNA callouts for selected details. Letters are equally spaced schematically; smooth connectors retain genomic anchors. For a short window, mode = "rows" shows all selected bases:

sequence_example <- plot_as3mt_alignseq(demo_dir, intron_factor = 30)
sequence_example$rows

Cai et al. tested otherwise matched two- and three-repeat human minigenes; three repeats produced more d2d3. This supports repeat-dependent splicing regulation, but does not establish sufficiency for the isoform’s evolutionary origin. The human allele experiment differs by 36 bp; the figure’s −72 bp marker instead compares the selected chimp and human references. Two base differences in the chimp homolog are context, not demonstrated causal SNVs.

3. RNA-seq and splice junctions

The bundled GTEx frontal-cortex (BA9) sample GTEX-15G19-0011-R10b-SM-7KUG4.1 has both exon-2/3 inclusion and E1→E4 skipping reads. Its recount3 BigWig contains total coverage; Snaptron supplies junction counts from the same sample. Both use GRCh38. geom_coverage() and geom_junction() follow the human exon/intron map automatically.

rna_example <- plot_as3mt_coverage(demo_dir, intron_factor = 30,
  junction_panel = "coverage")
rna_example$plot

Matched human coverage and splice-junction reads.

Arc labels are junction read counts: E1→E2, 9; E2→E3, 10; E3→E4, 11; E1→E4, 12. Line width reflects these counts. The layer takes exon-edge genomic anchors; it draws the curve and centres its label after compression. Choose panel = "coverage" to put arcs on the BigWig panel, or panel = "annotation" (the geom default) to put them on the gene model:

geom_junction(data = rna_example$junctions,
  aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend, height = height,
      linewidth = reads, label = reads, hjust = label_hjust, colour = event),
  panel = "coverage", inherit.aes = FALSE)

y and optional yend meet the measured coverage at the donor and acceptor exon bases. height controls the curve’s rise; staggered heights and text hjust separate the counts around narrow compressed introns. y, yend and height use the selected panel’s y units. For the gene-model layout, use plot_as3mt_alignseq(demo_dir, junction_panel = "annotation").

Source coverage values remain unchanged, and missing intervals are not filled. human-rnaseq-GTEX-15G19-provenance.json records the exact URLs, sample and extraction; data-raw/as3mt/prepare-gtex-rnaseq.py reproduces the snapshots. These short-read junctions support the splice events, not complete transcript abundances. This independent donor’s VNTR genotype is not inferred from the reference DNA or the separate minigene experiment.

Sources and reproducibility

  • Li et al. (2016), doi:10.1038/nm.4096: d2d3 reconstruction and repeat sequence.
  • Cai et al. (2021), doi:10.1093/schbul/sbaa098: human VNTR minigene comparison.
  • recount3 and Snaptron: matched GTEx coverage and exon-junction reads.

The installed extdata/as3mt directory contains the plotting helper, input snapshots and provenance. Repository preparation/export scripts are in data-raw/as3mt; the genomic ribbons use LASTZ --nogapped --chain blocks.

Combined result

The green RNA-seq signal and counted splice arcs occupy the same panel and share the human gene model’s compressed scale. Blue arcs support exon inclusion; the orange arc supports E1→E4 skipping. Purple outlines locate the VNTR; each species keeps its own DNA callout. Separate bars below the legend show exon and compressed-intron scales. The lower human transcript remains a paper-defined reconstruction; the repeat-count strip summarizes the tested human alleles schematically.

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(sequence_example$grob)
